src.label: USDA APHIS — pet travel from the United States to Ukraine (relaying Ukrainian rules)

head: Microchip, rabies vaccine and an antibody titer of 0.5 IU/ml taken over three months before export.
lines: The US agriculture department page on Ukrainian entry says personal dogs, cats and ferrets need an ISO microchip (or a pre-2011 tattoo) and an endorsed health certificate.

Pets over 12 weeks need a current rabies vaccine and a rabies titer of at least 0.5 IU/ml from an approved lab more than three months before export; the result stays valid while vaccination never lapses, and a lab copy goes with the certificate.

After a first vaccine, or a late booster, wait at least 21 days before travel. Pets of 12 to 16 weeks may travel if unvaccinated only under the no-wildlife-contact or vaccinated-mother conditions. This is a US-side relay.
